integrity: The infinite classification is proved by bounding factorial indices below the next prime, reducing every permitted composite factorial index, and using a unimodular prime-valuation matrix.
The asymptotic is a fixed-dimensional weighted-simplex lattice-point estimate.
The finite verifier is corroborative and is not used as a substitute for the infinite proof.
limitations: The prime-factorial normal form is proved only for largest prime divisor at most 11.
The witness 14! shows that the same nonnegative prime-factorial normal form fails at largest prime divisor 13.
Residual originality risk remains from potentially unindexed recreational or expository observations.
The 2007 paper was compared through publisher abstract and metadata rather than complete full text.
title: Prime-factorial normal forms for low-support Jordan–Pólya numbers
